\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{داوطلب} (dâvtalab)}{داوطلب (dâvtalab)}]{\fa{داوطلب} (dâvtalab) — a volunteer; a candidate}

\label{lesson:FA-C389-davtalab}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for consumption, then the Persian for to consume.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{داوطلب}}
\textbf{\fa{داوطلب}} (\emph{dâvtalab}) — \textquotedblleft{}a volunteer; a candidate\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{صد} \fa{داوطلب} \fa{بعد} \fa{از} \fa{زلزله} \fa{کمک} \fa{کردند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{sad dâvtalab ba'd az zelzele komak kardand.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
A hundred volunteers helped after the earthquake.
\end{quote}

Also an exam candidate. Plural \emph{dâvtalabân}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{داوطلب}} joins \emph{dâv} \textquotedblleft{}a turn, a stake\textquotedblright{}, a Persian word whose origin is not settled, to \emph{talab} \textquotedblleft{}seeking\textquotedblright{}, from Arabic \emph{ṭalab}: someone who seeks a turn.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for consumption, then the Persian for to consume, then say \emph{dâvtalab} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{خیریه} (kheyriye)}{خیریه (kheyriye)}]{\fa{خیریه} (kheyriye) — a charity}

\label{lesson:FA-C389-kheyriyye}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to consume, then the Persian for a volunteer.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{خیریه}}
\textbf{\fa{خیریه}} (\emph{kheyriye}) — \textquotedblleft{}a charity\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{هر} \fa{ماه} \fa{به} \fa{یک} \fa{خیریه} \fa{پول} \fa{میدهد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{u har mâh be yek kheyriye pul midahad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
She gives money to a charity every month.
\end{quote}

From \emph{kheyr} \textquotedblleft{}good\textquotedblright{}. As an adjective: \emph{mo'assese-ye kheyriye}, a charitable foundation.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{خیریه}} is built on \emph{kheyr} \textquotedblleft{}good\textquotedblright{}, borrowed from Arabic \emph{khayr} \textquotedblleft{}good, well\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), with the ending \emph{-iye}: a body that does good.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{صلح} (solh)}{صلح (solh)}]{\fa{صلح} (solh) — peace}

\label{lesson:FA-C389-solh}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a volunteer, then the Persian for a charity.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{صلح}}
\textbf{\fa{صلح}} (\emph{solh}) — \textquotedblleft{}peace\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{همه} \fa{مردم} \fa{صلح} \fa{میخواهند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{hame-ye mardom solh mikhâhand.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
All people want peace.
\end{quote}

The opposite is \emph{jang}, war. \emph{Solh kardan} — to make peace.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{صلح}} was borrowed from Arabic \emph{ṣulḥ} \textquotedblleft{}peace, reconciliation\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{خشونت} (khoshunat)}{خشونت (khoshunat)}]{\fa{خشونت} (khoshunat) — violence}

\label{lesson:FA-C389-khoshunat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a charity, then the Persian for peace.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{خشونت}}
\textbf{\fa{خشونت}} (\emph{khoshunat}) — \textquotedblleft{}violence\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{خشونت} \fa{هیچ} \fa{مشکلی} \fa{را} \fa{حل} \fa{نمیکند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{khoshunat hich moshkeli râ hal nemikonad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Violence does not solve any problem.
\end{quote}

\emph{Khoshunat-âmiz} — violent.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{خشونت}} was borrowed from Arabic \emph{khushūna} \textquotedblleft{}roughness, harshness\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB); in Persian it means violence.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{اعتیاد} (e'tiyâd)}{اعتیاد (e'tiyâd)}]{\fa{اعتیاد} (e'tiyâd) — addiction}

\label{lesson:FA-C389-etiyad}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for peace, then the Persian for violence.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{اعتیاد}}
\textbf{\fa{اعتیاد}} (\emph{e'tiyâd}) — \textquotedblleft{}addiction\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{اعتیاد} \fa{به} \fa{موبایل} \fa{بین} \fa{نوجوانها} \fa{زیاد} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{e'tiyâd be mobâyl beyn-e nojavânhâ ziyâd ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Addiction to mobile phones is common among teenagers.
\end{quote}

\emph{E'tiyâd be} — addiction to. \emph{Mo'tâd} — addicted.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{اعتیاد}} comes from Arabic \emph{i'tiyād} \textquotedblleft{}habit, familiarity\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB); in Persian a habit you cannot leave became an addiction.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
